messages:
Emma: quick async Q — noticed weirdness with POST /v1/generate when stop contains a prefix of the next token and max_tokens hits. responses sometimes include a trailing partial token in the last token text and logprobs seems inconsistent. anyone seen this?

Emma: example payload:
```json
{
  "model": "open-llama-13b",
  "prompt": "Write the word: appl",
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "stop": ["e"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```

Emma: expected: generator should either honor stop and return empty token (no partial) or truncate cleanly and logprob reflect truncated token. actual: returns token text "e" sometimes but logprobs show prob for "app" + partial.

Raj: hmm, sounds like edge of tokenization + streaming vs non-streaming. is this from streaming or normal call?

Emma: non-streaming. reproduced locally with runtime v2.3.1. filing because this affects our backwards compatibility assertions for gen param contract.

Oliver: fyi streaming path tries to cut on byte/utf boundaries differently, and we have a post-process that trims stop tokens but it runs before the logprob aggregation currently. could be ordering bug.

Sasha: suggestion: define precedence in API docs: 1) stop sequences are applied to generated text before truncation is committed to output, 2) max_tokens is a hard cap on raw model tokens — but we need to be explicit about whether returned logprobs correspond to raw tokens or to post-stop tokens.

Maria: +1 on definitive contract. for immediate mitigation can we add a regression test in runtime-integ that calls the endpoint with a deterministic tokenizer and asserts: returned_text does not contain partial stop suffixes and logprobs length matches tokens returned? I can draft test.

Emma: that'd be great. also want to check interplay with temperature/top_p: low temp but top_p high currently returns identical deterministic tokens in some models but the logprobs differ between runs. sounds like nondeterminism creeping in at decoder/sampling layer if we have async batching.

Raj: ping @Oliver — can you check batching/caching path? if we collapse requests, sometimes KV cache cutoff might yield different tokenization boundaries.

Oliver: will investigate. quick note: in one repro I saw `max_tokens` enforced post-sampling which was wrong — should cap raw sampling iterations. adding a unit to sampling loop now.

CI-bot: deploy queued: runtime/v2.3.2-tests (includes sampling-loop-fix) — build 3124 started.

Sasha: for API docs change, propose this text snippet to add to /docs/api/generation.md:
```text
Precedence: (1) The generation process runs token sampling up to max_tokens. (2) Stop sequences are applied to the concatenated generated text and any trailing stop sequence is removed from the returned text. (3) Logprobs correspond to the tokens actually returned after stop trimming.
```

Maria: that wording looks good, but step (2) needs clarification for partial-token stops (we should say stop matching is performed on the character/string level before token merging, and if a stop splits a token we trim the token and mark logprob as for the returned substring).

Raj: hmm that last bit about marking logprob for substring is tricky for some quantized tokenizers. alternative: disallow character-level stop matches that split tokens and document that stop must align to token boundaries for deterministic logprobs. which do we prefer?

Emma: prefer predictable behavior for users. I'd rather we document the requirement: stops should be token-aligned for deterministic logprobs, and if user supplies a stop that splits a token we guarantee we will still trim returned text but logprobs are undefined. at least it's explicit.

Oliver: implementation plan: 1) ensure sampling loop enforces max_tokens pre-stop, 2) run stop-trim after aggregation, 3) if stop splits token, set a flag in response `stop_truncated=true` and set logprobs to null for that token. will sketch PR.

Raj: sounds good. @Maria can you add integ tests for: token-aligned stop, char-split stop, streaming vs non-streaming parity, and deterministic low-temp runs?

Maria: yup, I'll open a PR with tests + doc update. planning to land before canary.

Emma: PRs please link here. also adding this to the genparams contract checklist for the next sprint. thanks all. :pray:

Raj: noted. tagging code review: #PR 4127 (sampling-loop fix), #PR 4131 (stop-trim & docs), #PR 4132 (integ tests).

Oliver: will review 4127 today.

CI-bot: build 3124 passed unit tests, running integration suite.

Emma: awesome — keeping this async so folks can grab reviews when available. if anyone hits a customer repro pls drop message and sample tokenization.

Sasha: ack, will update docs once PR lands. :memo:
